scope: Independent companion profiles; keep the frozen matrix and original expected labels. Each receipt is charged once regardless of aliases. CN PASS/FAIL/NOT_BUILT reflect the recorded standalone run or build; a bare failure without an attributable safety event is not evidence of the matching violation.

profiles.array_read_strong: Identical read definition, postcondition and input as the already measured CN array_load2 and its QCP read. The CN postcondition requires the full output map to equal the input map and the return to equal its indexed element. Six historical measurements serve 36 translations.
profiles.dll_add_strengthened: Typed allocated DLL nodes. The CN post now checks the new payload and each arm of QCP Dll. For n=NULL and element=0 the empty Dll(NULL,nil,0,nil) outcome is also legal. The original CN requires a nonempty singleton on this entry, and omits the payload equality. The companion checks the typed C allocation, including any padding that is outside QCP field-level assertions; comparison is confined to these typed fixtures. The C actions are token-identical across the two original CN variants.
profiles.dll_remove_strengthened: Typed allocated DLL nodes. Both contracts return ownership, the removed original payload, and the left/right value sequences. The companion also binds the returned node to the original next neighbor, else original previous neighbor, else NULL. The two original CN bodies are token-identical after proof-annotation removal. Comparison is confined to typed allocations; the CN object ownership can include padding.
profiles.array_client_entry_exit: Ordinary no-argument CN target with explicit return zero and an empty returned heap. Six original CN assertions are preserved. The called read contract follows the QCP helper (strong or weak). Interior assertions and local-array ownership encodings differ by QCP translation, so these are target-boundary comparisons only.
profiles.lifted_array_client: Client now receives an existing three-cell array with contents [0,1,2]. CN checks all three input cells, ownership and contents on exit, and return zero. The test driver owns the original local initializer. CN statement assertions and QCP local-resource assertions are not identical.
profiles.empty_heap_free: The original trusted helper is instrumented as an ordinary target with empty resource transfer at entry/exit. Original calls use the concrete nonzero pointer fixtures and free size unchanged. Debug tracing can confirm a runtime rejection when the normal CN reporter loses its source location.
profiles.empty_main_entry_exit: The original no-argument body is run as an ordinary target with an empty returned heap and return zero. The outer main only calls that target, so CN applies normal function-exit ownership checking.
profiles.runtime_client_entry_exit: Original concrete allocation client in an ordinary target; an empty returned heap is checked, with return-zero equality only when present in the QCP contract. Concrete allocator calls and original CN assertions are retained. Helper contracts, statement checks and transfer at external calls can differ; these targets must not be used as equal all-boundaries obligations.
profiles.original_fault_labels: No rerun or relabeling. Original Fulminate process diagnostics are compared with each strategy's original teSpec safety classification. Only matching access types with an explicit runtime diagnostic count as the same fault.
